scope: Reviewed all 17 files: src/ harness, tools, sub-agents, checkpoint, audit; prompts/system.md; config/agent.yaml; Dockerfile; requirements.txt; k8s/ manifests; .github/CODEOWNERS; README.md. Not found: .brace/ records, CI workflows (release.yml referenced but absent), IAM/Terraform for the AWS role, S3 bucket policy, drift tooling, alert routing, tests. Not a git repo, so no commit. No .mcp.json; no MCP.

evidence.note: _run uses subprocess.run(command, shell=True); kubectl args like 'get pods; <any command>' run any program in the image
helm() has no subcommand allowlist at all
allowed_binaries is never read by any code; the comment 'Anything else is refused' is not enforced
dispatcher does reject unknown tool names

findings.summary: The tool allowlist exists by name, but shell=True and an unrestricted helm tool let the model run any program in the container.
findings.next_step: Replace shell=True with argument lists, enforce allowed_binaries and a helm verb list in code, write a tool inventory with task reasons, then run recipe B01.

evidence.note: ClusterRoleBinding ops-agent-admin binds the agent ServiceAccount to cluster-admin
automountServiceAccountToken: true with that cluster-admin role
GitHub access uses a PAT (key github-pat), scope not visible
/ops handler runs for any Slack user; no check of requester permissions

findings.summary: The agent holds cluster-admin in its namespace's cluster and any Slack user can direct it.
findings.next_step: Replace cluster-admin with namespaced Roles listing verbs and resources, scope the GitHub credential to named repos, authorize requesters, then run recipe B02.

evidence.note: GITHUB_TOKEN is a static PAT from a Kubernetes Secret
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and SLACK_BOT_TOKEN are static secrets with no rotation or expiry shown
PAT placed in git process env for every git call, including ones the model directs

findings.summary: Long-lived static tokens are used where short-lived GitHub App or federated tokens exist, and no expiry or rotation is defined.
findings.next_step: Move GitHub to short-lived GitHub App installation tokens, document lifetimes and rotation, add secret scanning, then run recipe B03.

evidence.note: dedicated ServiceAccount ops-agent could be unbound independently of Slack users
GitHub PAT may belong to a person; revoking it could cut that person off

findings.summary: A separate Kubernetes identity exists, but no revocation procedure, token lifetime, or cutoff time is defined.
findings.next_step: Run recipe B04 timed drill: revoke the ServiceAccount binding and the GitHub token, measure cutoff on open sessions.

evidence.note: kubectl verbs include delete, apply, scale, rollout with no approval step
git push allowed; 'push --force' passes the first-word check
dispatch has no approval gate for any operation
helm uninstall/upgrade allowed without any check
system prompt authorizes force-push; deletion rules are prompt-only (line 7)

findings.summary: No high-impact operation is gated; the agent reads untrusted logs, holds cluster-admin, and pushes to GitHub with no approval anywhere.
findings.next_step: Add an execution-path gate that blocks delete, apply, scale, helm uninstall/upgrade/rollback, and git push (especially --force) pending a specific human approval; cover the shell path; then run recipe B05.

evidence.note: no approval record, binding, expiry, or single-use logic exists anywhere

findings.summary: There is no approval mechanism, so none of the approval integrity properties exist while B05 needs approvals.
findings.next_step: Build approvals bound to instance, operation, target, args hash, approver, expiry, single use, fail-closed; then run recipe B06.

evidence.note: while True loop with no turn, time, token-total, or cost cap
spawn_worker starts processes with no count or depth limit; workers can spawn workers
only per-call max_output_tokens is set

findings.summary: Runs and worker spawning are unbounded.
findings.next_step: Add max turns, wall-clock limit, cost cap, worker count and depth caps, and per-user/fleet quotas; then run recipe B07.

evidence.note: policyTypes [Ingress] only; egress unrestricted
cluster-admin gives reach to every namespace and secret in the cluster
agent works in production clusters; isolation only stated in prompt rules

findings.summary: No infrastructure boundary limits which systems the agent reaches; it has admin reach into production.
findings.next_step: Write the list of reachable systems, add egress NetworkPolicy and namespaced RBAC, then run recipe B08.

evidence.note: no Egress policy type, so all egress including 169.254.169.254 is allowed
shell injection gives curl-free but python-capable outbound paths

findings.summary: There is no egress allowlist.
findings.next_step: Add default-deny egress with allowed peers (Anthropic, Slack, GitHub, S3, cluster API servers) and block metadata addresses; then run recipe B09.

findings.next_step: Run recipe B10: confirm release.yml produces SBOM and provenance, Kyverno and cosign versions, policy mode in cluster, and unsigned/wrong-repo images are rejected.
